newsitem.title: UK: Saunders pleased by EU court ruling - consultant.
newsitem.headline: Saunders pleased by EU court ruling - consultant.

text.p: George Devlin, human rights consultant to former Guinness chairman Ernest Saunders said Saunders is "extremely pleased" by the decision of the European Court of Human Rights which earlier ruled that Britain had denied him a fair trial.

"We are extremely pleased at the outcome and extremely pleased that the European court upheld Mr Saunders' claim that he had an unfair trial and that his trial breeched article six of the European Convention of European Rights that stipulates that everyone in the UK is entitled to a fair trial," said Devlin.

He added that the government will now be required to amend company law accordingly. Saunders said that he was unfairly convicted because evidence obtained by Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) inspectors under compulsion was used in court.

Saunders was convicted in 1990 on 12 counts including false accounting and theft for artificially inflating Guinness's share price to help its 1986 takeover of Distillers prevail against rival bidder Argyll Plc.
The European Court of Human Rights ruling casts doubt on the DTI's methods of investigating alleged corporate corruption in Britain, where suspects have no right to silence.
The Serious Fraud Office as well as DTI Inspectors have wide powers to persuade suspects to answer questions.
The European Court however rejected Saunders' claim for 4.6 million pounds in compensation for lost earnings but ordered the British government to pay him 75,000 pounds in legal costs.
